text: Back in lesson four, we decided the field team lives in Tableau, not Power BI — so now we rebuild the same churn view there, in Tableau's own language.

The temptation is to translate the DAX measures line by line. Don't. Tableau thinks in row-level data and LOD expressions, not filter context, so the classification gets rebuilt using FIXED level-of-detail expressions — one evaluation per customer, no matter what's on the view.

Two FIXED LOD fields do the real work: one finds each customer's last qualifying order date, the other counts their purchases in the trailing twelve months — both tied to a Tableau Parameter, so the whole view can re-run against any as-of date.

From those two fields, a Customer Status calculation sorts everyone into Active, Churned, Never Purchased, or Not Yet Retained — the exact same definition as the SQL and DAX builds, just written the way Tableau actually wants to think.

Two worksheets mirror the Power BI pages — churn rate ranked by region, and a region-by-segment breakdown — combined into one dashboard. Before any of it reaches the field team, the Tableau number has to match Power BI's within rounding.
A mismatch here means a logic bug to fix, not two valid opinions about the same customers. Next up: an independent Excel check before anyone else sees these numbers.
